title: EU region affinity break causes failover to incompatible low-capacity model
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: During an autoscale/burst event for a large EU Dedicated customer, a portion of production requests were routed to a compatible-seeming hosted fallback model in US region that had an incompatible tokenization/profile (legacy 8-bit quant variant). This produced garbled structured outputs and raised a high-severity customer escalation. We observed misroutes across Hosted, Dedicated and Private instances due to a region-affinity cache invalidation race coupled with the fallback comparator selecting a lower-tier model because of an ordering bug in policy merge logic.

Impact: Affected customers experienced incorrect chat/structured output (JSON schema violations) for ~12 minutes. Error rate on the customer tenant spiked to 9% of requests; SLO alerts triggered and support received multiple escalations. No data exfiltration suspected; outputs were incorrect but non-sensitive.

Root cause hypothesis: Two contributing issues identified so far: 1) The region-affinity hint cache entry for the tenant was invalidated during a scale event and subsequent policy lookup fell back to global policy path that included Hosted fallback entries. 2) The fallback comparator applies a string-based comparator on model variant ids under certain merge conditions; because legacy-quant variants had IDs that sort earlier, they were chosen over a region-compatible lower-latency shard. Additionally, an oversight in the compatibility filter allowed fallbacks whose tokenizer/config mismatched the requested model family.

Repro steps (internal):
1) Simulate Dedicated pool drain + canary routing for tenant eu-tenant-004 with capacity spike.
2) Force region-affinity cache TTL eviction and trigger routing resolution under high QPS.
3) Observe policy merge order and comparator decision; confirm selection of hosted fallback model us-legacy-8q instead of eu-dedicated-01-compatible.

Immediate mitigation taken:
- Rolled back the recent routing cache TTL change in staging and applied a hotfix to increase tenant-affinity TTL for EU tenants (10m -> 60m) while we investigate.
- Updated canary routing rule to prefer same-region Dedicated pools for tenants with Dedicated assignments.
- Notified impacted customer via CSM and support; offered audit logs and produced immediate temp policy pin (tenant-scoped) to force correct model mapping.

Short-term fix plan (this ticket):
- Patch policy merge to enforce explicit compatibility filter before comparator ordering. (owner: Mateo Ruiz)
- Add guardrail that excludes model variants with incompatible tokenizer/embedding dim from fallback set.
- Adjust comparator to weight region-matching and capacity class above lexicographic id ordering.
- Backfill unit/integration tests that simulate TTL eviction + autoscale race.

Long-term actions (follow-ups):
- ENG-70401: formalize model variant compatibility schema and add pre-deploy model metadata checks.
- ENG-70122 and ENG-69901: revisit global routing cache semantics and introduce stronger invariants for tenant affinity.
- Console: expose tenant-level last-known-region and fallback reasoning in the trace UI (product ticket).

Monitoring and verification:
- Dashboard: created temporary panel to show tenant-level route decisions, comparator score breakdown, and model-tokenizer signature mismatches. Link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/route-debug/tenant-routes?orgId=1
- SLO: monitor spikes in schema-violation errors and tokenization errors; rollforward only after 30m stable and no elevated error rates.

Stakeholders notified: CSM (Lina Zhao), Support lead (Evan Brooks), Head of Infra (Priya Menon), Oncall Routing (SRE-rotation).

2026-03-05: Draft patch implemented in routing comparator to enforce compatibility pre-filter (WIP).
